passages.original: 41. Videte tamen, obsecro, quale sit, ideo volenti et currenti misericordiam Dei nun esse necessariam, quae illum etiam prævenit, ut curreret, quia de quodam ait Apostolus, Quod vult faciat : ibi, ut arbitror, ubi sequitur et dicit, Non peccat, si nubat. Quasi pro magno habendum sit, velle nubere, ubi de adjutorio divinae misericordix opcrosius disputatur. Aut vero etiam ibi prodest aliquid velle, nisi Deus providentia, qua gubernat omnia, marem feminamque conjungat. Aut quoniam ad Philemonem scripsit Apostulus, Ut non quasi ex necessitate bonum ejus esset, sed voluntarium : quasi aliter sit voluntarium bonum, nisi cum Deus operatur in nobis et velle et operari, pro bona voluntate (Philipp. 11, 13).
passages.english: 41. But see, I beg you, what sort of [argument] it is [to say] that the mercy of God is not necessary for one who wills and runs, [the mercy] which even goes before him so that he may run, on the ground that the Apostle says of a certain man, "Let him do what he wills": in the place, I think, where he goes on and says, "He does not sin if he marries." As if willing to marry were to be held a great matter, when the help of divine mercy is being discussed with such labour. Or indeed as if even there willing were of any use, unless God, by the providence with which he governs all things, joins male and female together. Or [on the ground] that the Apostle wrote to Philemon, "So that your good might not be as if from necessity, but voluntary": as if a good were voluntary in any other way than when God works in us both to will and to work, according to [his] good will (Phil. 2:13).
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected: "nun" for "non", "misericordix" for "misericordiae", "opcrosius" for "operosius", "Apostulus" for "Apostolus"; the reference "Philipp. 11, 13" should be Phil. 2:13. "Aut vero etiam ibi prodest" is read as a sarcastic "as if" continuing the preceding "quasi". "Pro bona voluntate" may refer to God's good will or to the human good will; the Latin is ambiguous.
